LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Greetings Suggested vocabulary Good morning, good afternoon, hello, good evening
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Greetings Suggested vocabulary Good morning, good afternoon, hello, good evening in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we greet people? 2. How do we greet people at different times of the day?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to recreate learning experiences outside the class is enhanced as they use

vocabulary learnt to greet people at different times of the day.

Values:
• Unity: is developed as the learner takes turn to greet each other with peers and appreciate the importance of oneness regardless of

individual differences.

• Respect:is developed as the learner practises patience and humility with each other during turn taking as they greet.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills(Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they practice different types of greetings.
